chapters.title: The Boast of Sablyanos
chapters.html:
3 Meqabyan 1

The One Who Will Come

1The coasts of Egypt will rejoice in the last days, because of the Good and Gentle One who comes to them, who will take vengeance for the oppression and the deceit of Sablyanos, who opposes the way of his Creator.

2He will take vengeance on him and bring his honor down into the earth and into shame, for he exalted himself in his thoughts.

What the Deceiver Says

3He said, "Who is higher than I? I go into the heart of the seas and go up to the heights, I look on the depths, and I strike down the children of Adam like young birds.

4No one keeps them from my hand, for I do not spare those who live on the earth if they do the will of God. I devise pretexts against them, to turn them aside from the straight way of God,

5and to bring them into my wicked way, so that they go with me into perdition.

6Because of this, those who love Him and keep His commandment hate me; but those who stray from their Lord come to me, love me, keep my covenant and do my commandment as I command them. For I harm their hearts and twist their thoughts, so that they do not turn back to God their Creator.

7When I show them the goods of the world, I lead their hearts astray from the straight way; when I show them lovely women and virgins, by these too I turn them aside from the straight way.

8When I show them the gleaming stones of India, and stones of gold and silver, by this too I turn them aside from the straight way, so that they turn to my deeds.

9When I show them garments of fine linen and byssus, silk and brocade and ʾagāyāt, by this too I turn them from the straight way and bring them into my thoughts; and when I show them possessions and cattle like the sand, by this too I turn them to my deeds.

10When I show them the rivalries of pride, of women, of rank and of wrath, by all this I turn them to my way.

11When I show them omens, I enter into the hearts of their companions and mingle into their hearts the words of their own omens; I show them the omen of their own word, and so I make fools of them.

12To those whom I have made my dwelling I show signs, whether by the courses of the stars, the movements of the clouds, the burning of fire, or the cries of birds and beasts. By all this I set a sign in their hearts, for they are my dwelling.

13They speak and give signs to their companions, and I go before them and become the sign, as their soothsayers told them.

14I make the sign of their word come true for them, so that those who consulted them go astray and give them a reward, and tell their companions, saying, 'There are no seers like so-and-so, man or woman; it happens to them as they spoke. They know prophecy and can tell good from evil; everything happens as they said, and it is done as they spoke.'

15When they say this, I rejoice that those who perish multiply and those who go astray through me increase, so that the children of Adam perish with me. For because of their father Adam, God threw me down from my throne, because I said, 'I will not bow down to one lower than me.'

The Deceiver's Plea

16I too draw into perdition all his children who walk in my commandment; and I have a grant from Him who created me, that those I lead astray will be cast with me into the fire.

17I pleaded with my Lord when He brought down His wrath on me and commanded them to bind me and cast me into Gehenna and the depths of Sheol. When my Creator commanded this, I pleaded before Him, saying, 'My Lord, since You are angry with me, have rebuked me with Your punishment and struck me in Your wrath, allow me to speak one word before You.'

18My Lord answered me and said to me, 'Speak, and I will hear you.' At once I took hold and begged Him, saying, 'Since I have been driven from my throne, let those I have led astray be with me in what I suffer.

19But those who refused me and did not go astray through me, and did not keep my commandment, so that they do Your commandment, fulfill Your will and keep Your word, when they refused what I taught them and did not go astray through me as I led them astray, let them be for Your kingdom, and let them receive the crown You gave me when You loved me.

20To all the powers who were driven out with me, who are called satans, give their crowns, and seat them at Your right hand on my throne, which is left empty by me and my angels.

21Let them praise You as You wish, and be as I was and as my angels were; let them praise You as You wish. For my authority has been overthrown and theirs raised up, for You hated me and loved those created from earth and dust.'

22My Lord answered me and said to me, 'As you wish: those who do not want what is Mine, let them be yours, according to your word; for though they saw and heard, you led them astray.

23Their perishing does not grieve Me, when they come to you, having left My commandment and the word of My Scriptures; if you led them astray, they will be condemned with you in punishment.

24You have no way out forever and ever, you and those who went astray through you, in the judgment of punishment; you will be tormented in the fire forever and ever.'"

Notes

  • The text — the Ge'ez of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo printed Bible, and the verse numbers follow it. No other ancient text of the book is known, and it is not the Greek 3 Maccabees. Much of it is the deceiver's own speech and the prophet's answer to him.

  • v1 "The coasts of Egypt will rejoice… the Good and Gentle One who comes to them" — Behold, the LORD is riding on a swift cloud and comes to Egypt (Isaiah 19:1). Sablyanos is the teacher of evil of 1 Meqabyan 13:3 and 17:3–5 and 2 Meqabyan 9:2.

  • v3 "Who is higher than I? I go into the heart of the seas" — the boast of the king of Babylon, I will ascend above the heights of the clouds (Isaiah 14:14), and of the prince of Tyre, I sit in the seat of the gods, in the heart of the seas (Ezekiel 28:2).

  • v9 the garments — fine linen, purple cloth, silk and scarlet cloth among the wares of Babylon (Revelation 18:12). ʾAgāyāt is a cloth not otherwise known.

  • vv11–14 omens and soothsayers — There shall not be found among you… anyone who practices divination or tells fortunes or interprets omens… a medium or a necromancer (Deuteronomy 18:10–11).

  • v15 "I will not bow down to one lower than me" — the fall of the devil for refusing to worship Adam, as in 2 Meqabyan 9:3 and the Life of Adam and Eve 13–14.

  • v19 — the Ge'ez says twice, wa-ʾi-saḥtu bəya za-kama ʾasḥatkəwwomu, and did not go astray through me as I led them astray; the repeated clause is rendered once.

  • vv19–21 "let them receive the crown You gave me… seat them on my throne" — the thrones left empty by the fallen angels given to the righteous; God's answer at 2:1, I will make them inherit your throne.

  • v22 "those who do not want what is Mine" — the Ge'ez has la-mbārya, a word not otherwise known; read with the sense of the verse.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Prophet Answers the Deceiver
chapters.html:
3 Meqabyan 2

God's Word and the Deceiver's Reply

1"But those you could not overcome, like My servant Job, I will make inherit your throne in honor; to those you could not lead astray I will give the kingdom of heaven as a reward," said God, who rules all.

2"But I will press the children of Adam hard in everything, and will not let them stand in good deeds, if I am able to lead them astray. For I press the children of Adam in everything, and make the desire of the world sweet to them,

3whether by the desire for food, the desire for drink and the love of garments, or by the love of talk, of giving and of taking;

4or by the love of looking, the love of hearing, the love of walking and wandering about; or by much talk in pride, and the love of sleep and dreams;

5or by much drinking and drunkenness; or by the sight of the beauty of the women of this world and the scent of perfumes, I lead them astray;

6or by slandering their neighbor in hatred; or by the sight of the beauty of the women of this world and the scent of perfumes, I lead them astray.

7By all this I oppose them, so that they cannot be saved, and I drive them from the way of God, so that they go with me into perdition, for whose sake I was driven from my throne."

The Prophet's Rebuke

8The prophet said, "You perdition and destroyer, do you exalt yourself so over the creature of God, when you transgressed the commandment of God in your pride, in the hardness of your heart, in angering your Creator and not praising your God?

9When your Creator was angry with you, He cast you down because of your evil deeds. Why then do you oppress the poor one whom his God created from earth and dust, made as He willed and set there for His praise?

10You, a spirit, grew proud at the word of God, who created you from flame of fire and wind.

11When you boasted, God saw your evil deeds and created a singer in your place, to praise His name without weariness; for you, with your demons, transgressed the commandment of God.

12He made Adam too, with his children, to praise the name of God in place of your praise and that of your host, whom God rejected because of your pride. For you exalted yourself above all the angels, above the hosts of angels who were like you.

13Because of this God tore you away from all the archangels who were like you, and your hosts too, who were created with you; with one counsel you strayed from the praise of God, through the hardness of your hearts and the pride of your thoughts, which is of no use. You exalted yourselves over your Creator, and not over another.

Adam and Eve

14Because of this, so that He might be praised by the lowly, He created Adam from the dust of the earth, and gave him a law and a commandment not to eat of the fruit of the tree.

15He set him over all that He had made and taught him, saying, 'Eat of every tree in the garden; but of one tree, the sting of death, do not eat of it, so that you do not bring death on your own head.'

16When you heard this word, you spat venom from your mouth on Eve, the bone of Adam's side.

17You stole the pure lamb by evil cunning, so that she was made like you, a transgressor of the commandment.

18You led astray Eve, who was created gentle as a dove and did not know your ways; you led her astray with your crooked word and your cunning speech. After you led astray that first creature, she went and led astray the creature of God, the first man, who was created from earth.

19In your pride you entangled him in what was not fitting, in turmoil, and made him transgress the word of his Creator; in your pride you scorched the poor man.

20By your wickedness you drew him far from the love of his God; by your pretext you drove him out of the garden of delight; by your snare you made him leave the food of the garden.

21By your lie you made him thirst, cut off from the drink of the garden. For you were hostile from the beginning to the gentle creature, to bring him down into your death, into Sheol, and to take him from the love of his God, who brought him from where he was not into true being.

22Though he was of earth, He made him spiritual and able to speak, one who praises and sings to his God with his soul, his body and his mind.

23He created for him [words lost]

Notes

  • v1 "those you could not overcome, like My servant Job" — Have you considered My servant Job, that there is none like him on the earth… he still holds fast his integrity (Job 1:8; 2:3). The second clause has la-ʾənki, a copying slip; read with the sense of the first, those you could not lead astray.

  • v2 "if I am able" — the Ge'ez has kəhəlka, "if you are able," in the deceiver's own speech; read as kəhəlku, "if I am able."

  • v6 — the second half repeats the end of verse 5 word for word in the Ge'ez; it is rendered as written.

  • v10 "flame of fire and wind" — He makes His angels winds, His ministers a flaming fire (Psalm 104:4). The words rendered at the word of God could also be read "in calling himself God."

  • v15 "the sting of death" — the Ge'ez šok mot is "the thorn of death"; O death, where is your sting? (1 Corinthians 15:55). You shall not eat of it, for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die (Genesis 2:17).

  • v17 "the pure lamb" — Eve, as the next verse makes plain. The verb rendered stole is uncertain.

  • v18 — The serpent was more crafty than any other beast… she took of its fruit and ate, and she also gave some to her husband (Genesis 3:1, 6); be wise as serpents and innocent as doves (Matthew 10:16).

  • v20 — two of the three verbs have the form "she," as though Eve did these things through the deceiver; they are rendered with you like the middle one.

  • v23 — the text breaks off here; the rest of the verse is lost.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Comfort Outside the Garden
chapters.html:
3 Meqabyan 3

Adam's Thoughts and the Deceiver's

1"But for you [words lost]

2But to Adam [words lost]

3Moreover, they have restless thoughts, like the waves of the sea, like a whirlwind that lifts dust from the earth, like a sea wave beaten by the wind, and like drops of rain that cannot be counted. So are the thoughts of Adam, from the many thoughts in his heart that cannot be counted.

4But you have one mind and no other, for you are not of flesh.

5Yet you destroyed him who [words lost]

Out of the Garden

6She came and led astray the first creature of God by eating of the tree, and brought death on herself and on her children, because she transgressed the commandment of her Creator.

7By the judgment of God's justice they went out of the garden; yet He did not keep them far from the garden in enmity, but comforted them in the land into which He drove them, with their children, the fruit of their womb and the fruit of their land.

8When you drove them out of the garden in envy, God gave them green shoots, sabawwota, from the trees of the garden, so that they might plant them and be comforted by the fruit of the garden and the fruit of the earth that God gave them,

9so that they would be comforted and renew their hearts greatly by seeing children, by seeing the garden, and by the fruit of the earth, which the earth made sprout from the dust. When they eat it, they are greatly comforted from the sorrow of your driving them out of the garden.

10They are comforted in their hearts by their children and by the fruit of the earth, for God knows how to comfort His creature.

11He renews their hearts with food and water, for they had been driven out into this land of thorns and thistles."

Notes

  • vv1, 2, 5 — the text breaks off in each of these verses; the rest is lost. Verse 2 keeps one more word, təwəhbu, "given," whose sense cannot be recovered without what came before it.

  • v3 "like the waves of the sea" — the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea that is driven and tossed by the wind (James 1:6).

  • v7 "they went out of the garden" — the LORD God sent him out from the garden of Eden to work the ground from which he was taken (Genesis 3:23).

  • v8 sabawwota — a word not otherwise known; it may be a form of "seven," but that is not certain.

  • v11 "a land of thorns and thistles" — thorns and thistles it shall bring forth for you… By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread (Genesis 3:18–19).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Pride and Repentance
chapters.html:
3 Meqabyan 4

The Throne Taken Away

1"Adam's Lord is there to redeem him; He will put you to shame and rescue the lamb from the hand of the wolf.

2But those you have made your own will rise and be drawn with you into perdition.

3Those who kept the law of the Lord their God will rejoice with their Creator, those whom God hid from your evil deeds, to make them His portion, so that they may praise Him with His holy angels, who did not transgress the law of their God as you did.

4But because of your pride the Most High God took from you the throne He had given you above all who were like you, so that you might praise Him with His angels.

5You refused, and you were named, and they were named, demons. Those who love God will be a people to Him like the holy angels, the cherubim and seraphim who praise Him, spreading their wings without ceasing.

6Those who love God will be a people to Him like the holy angels, the cherubim and seraphim who praise Him, spreading their wings without ceasing.

7But by your trickery and your pride you lost your praise, which He commanded you to give Him at all times with your tribe and all your company, who were created with you in your fellowship.

8When you forgot the praise of Him who created you, you thought He could not make another like you, so that the praise of God who created you would not cease: a tenth tribe, when you were cut off from the company of your brothers, so that the praise of God your Creator would not cease.

9In the pride of your heart you grew slack in the praise of Him who created you; He was angry with you, laughed at you, and bound you in the terror of Gehenna with your demons.

Adam Made in Your Place

10He took earth from the ground in His holy hands, mixed in water, fire and wind, and created Adam in His own image and likeness.

11He set him over all the work of His hands, to fill up His praise where you had fallen short; the praise of the earthly one was joined to the praise of the heavenly ones and became equal to it.

12But through your pride and your stiff neck you were driven out, and cut yourself off from the praise of God who created you.

13Know that His praise did not grow less, for He made one to praise Him by the counsel of His will, so that the praise of God would not grow less.

14He knows everything before it is. He knew before He created you that you would transgress His commandment, and that you would lead Adam to transgress, His servant made in His image and likeness; for before the world there was a hidden counsel with Him.

15As Solomon said, 'Before the hills He brought me forth; before the world was formed He created me, before the foundations of the earth were laid,

16before He set the mountains and hills in their places, before the paths of the world were made firm, before the light of the sun and moon shone, before the circling of the stars and the seasons were,

17before night and day took their turns, before the waves of the sea were, before all that has come to be came to be,

18before what now appears appeared, before every name now named was named.' It was not you, nor those like you, who were in the thought of God, but Adam His servant.

19When you transgressed, He acted so that His holy name would be praised; when you grew proud, He created Adam His servant, so that He would be praised by a lowly one, His own work, whom He created from earth.

20For God hears the prayer of the poor from afar, and God loves the praise of the lowly.

21God loathes the talk of the proud, for He does not delight in the strength of the horse, nor take pleasure in the legs of a man; God takes pleasure in those who fear Him.

He Repented; You Did Not

22They weep and wail for the sins they have done.

23But you could not bow down in repentance.

24He, though he was earth, turned back in repentance, weeping and lamenting for his sin before God his Creator.

25But you, in the pride of your heart and the stiffness of your neck, did not know the way of peace or of repentance, and could not bow down before God your Creator in repentance, weeping and tears.

26He, earth and dust and poor, turned with weeping and tears to repentance, to the way of peace and to humility.

27But you did not humble yourself, nor bend your heart to Him who created you.

28He humbled himself, bowed down for the sin he had committed, and was not proud.

29Nor was the error his own making; it came from you. For you created rebellion and planted its root, and in your pride you drew him with you into perdition.

30He Himself knows that it came about through the pride of your heart, for before He created the two of you He knew you and knew your ways.

31As for him, who had no pride of his own devising, He brought him back in repentance, weeping and tears.

32But in the pride of your heart you could not bow down in repentance. For one who sins and bows down has made his pride worse than his first offense; but one who sins, bows down and weeps before God his Creator,

33he is the one who has truly repented and found the way of his salvation, so as to soften the heart of his Lord. He has bowed down before his Master, and his Lord turns from His earlier resolve to be angry with His servant, for he has bowed before Him with much repentance and prostration; He forgives him his former sin,

34if he does not go back to his former offense. This is his complete repentance, if he does this. Adam did not forget to think of his God, and bowed down in repentance to Him who created him.

35You too, bow down to Him and repent before Him who created you, and do not bring guilt on him and on the work of His hands. For their Lord who created them knows their weakness, for they are flesh and blood.

36Once their soul goes out of their body, it becomes dust until the day He has chosen.

Notes

  • v1 "rescue the lamb from the hand of the wolf" — I will rescue My flock; they shall no longer be a prey (Ezekiel 34:22).

  • v6 — repeats the second half of verse 5 word for word in the Ge'ez; it is rendered as written.

  • v8 "a tenth tribe" — Ethiopian tradition counts the angels in ten orders; when the deceiver's order fell, Adam's race was made to fill the tenth place. The verse is hard to follow in the Ge'ez and is rendered close to its order.

  • v10 "mixed in water, fire and wind" — Adam made of the four elements, earth, water, fire and wind, as in the Ethiopian teaching on creation; the LORD God formed the man of dust from the ground (Genesis 2:7).

  • vv15–18 "Before the hills He brought me forth" — Wisdom's words in Proverbs 8:23–29. The verb rendered formed in v15 (yəṭāʿṭāʿ) is not otherwise known.

  • v18 "but Adam His servant" — the Ge'ez has "and Adam His servant"; read as "but," which the verse needs.

  • vv20–21 — He does not forget the cry of the afflicted (Psalm 9:12); His delight is not in the strength of the horse, nor His pleasure in the legs of a man, but the LORD takes pleasure in those who fear Him (Psalm 147:10–11).

  • v29 — after "into perdition" the Ge'ez has ʾiʾaka, a word not understood; it is left out.

  • v32 "one who sins and bows down has made his pride worse" — the sense needs "does not bow down," as the rest of the verse shows, but there is no "not" in the Ge'ez; it is rendered as written.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

speech.text: 3 Meqabyan 4
The Throne Taken Away
"Adam's Lord is there to redeem him; He will put you to shame and rescue the lamb from the hand of the wolf.
But those you have made your own will rise and be drawn with you into perdition.

Those who kept the law of the Lord their God will rejoice with their Creator, those whom God hid from your evil deeds, to make them His portion, so that they may praise Him with His holy angels, who did not transgress the law of their God as you did.
But because of your pride the Most High God took from you the throne He had given you above all who were like you, so that you might praise Him with His angels.

You refused, and you were named, and they were named, demons. Those who love God will be a people to Him like the holy angels, the cherubim and seraphim who praise Him, spreading their wings without ceasing.
Those who love God will be a people to Him like the holy angels, the cherubim and seraphim who praise Him, spreading their wings without ceasing.
But by your trickery and your pride you lost your praise, which He commanded you to give Him at all times with your tribe and all your company, who were created with you in your fellowship.

When you forgot the praise of Him who created you, you thought He could not make another like you, so that the praise of God who created you would not cease: a tenth tribe, when you were cut off from the company of your brothers, so that the praise of God your Creator would not cease.
In the pride of your heart you grew slack in the praise of Him who created you; He was angry with you, laughed at you, and bound you in the terror of Gehenna with your demons.
Adam Made in Your Place
He took earth from the ground in His holy hands, mixed in water, fire and wind, and created Adam in His own image and likeness.
He set him over all the work of His hands, to fill up His praise where you had fallen short; the praise of the earthly one was joined to the praise of the heavenly ones and became equal to it.
But through your pride and your stiff neck you were driven out, and cut yourself off from the praise of God who created you.
Know that His praise did not grow less, for He made one to praise Him by the counsel of His will, so that the praise of God would not grow less.

He knows everything before it is. He knew before He created you that you would transgress His commandment, and that you would lead Adam to transgress, His servant made in His image and likeness; for before the world there was a hidden counsel with Him.
As Solomon said, 'Before the hills He brought me forth; before the world was formed He created me, before the foundations of the earth were laid,
before He set the mountains and hills in their places, before the paths of the world were made firm, before the light of the sun and moon shone, before the circling of the stars and the seasons were,
before night and day took their turns, before the waves of the sea were, before all that has come to be came to be,
before what now appears appeared, before every name now named was named.' It was not you, nor those like you, who were in the thought of God, but Adam His servant.

When you transgressed, He acted so that His holy name would be praised; when you grew proud, He created Adam His servant, so that He would be praised by a lowly one, His own work, whom He created from earth.
For God hears the prayer of the poor from afar, and God loves the praise of the lowly.
God loathes the talk of the proud, for He does not delight in the strength of the horse, nor take pleasure in the legs of a man; God takes pleasure in those who fear Him.
He Repented; You Did Not
They weep and wail for the sins they have done.
But you could not bow down in repentance.
He, though he was earth, turned back in repentance, weeping and lamenting for his sin before God his Creator.
But you, in the pride of your heart and the stiffness of your neck, did not know the way of peace or of repentance, and could not bow down before God your Creator in repentance, weeping and tears.
He, earth and dust and poor, turned with weeping and tears to repentance, to the way of peace and to humility.
But you did not humble yourself, nor bend your heart to Him who created you.
He humbled himself, bowed down for the sin he had committed, and was not proud.
Nor was the error his own making; it came from you. For you created rebellion and planted its root, and in your pride you drew him with you into perdition.
He Himself knows that it came about through the pride of your heart, for before He created the two of you He knew you and knew your ways.
As for him, who had no pride of his own devising, He brought him back in repentance, weeping and tears.

But in the pride of your heart you could not bow down in repentance. For one who sins and bows down has made his pride worse than his first offense; but one who sins, bows down and weeps before God his Creator,

he is the one who has truly repented and found the way of his salvation, so as to soften the heart of his Lord. He has bowed down before his Master, and his Lord turns from His earlier resolve to be angry with His servant, for he has bowed before Him with much repentance and prostration; He forgives him his former sin,
if he does not go back to his former offense. This is his complete repentance, if he does this. Adam did not forget to think of his God, and bowed down in repentance to Him who created him.

You too, bow down to Him and repent before Him who created you, and do not bring guilt on him and on the work of His hands. For their Lord who created them knows their weakness, for they are flesh and blood.
Once their soul goes out of their body, it becomes dust until the day He has chosen.

chapters.title: Weigh Your Deeds
chapters.html:
3 Meqabyan 5

Earth Returns to Earth

1Know Him who created you, and do not forget Him who strengthened and saved you, the Holy One of Israel. For though you were earth, He made you in His image and likeness and placed you in the garden, to delight in it and to work the land.

2When you transgressed His commandment, He drove you out from there into this dry land, a land of thorns and thistles, which He cursed because of you.

3For you are earth and it is earth; you are dust and it is dust; you are soil and it is soil. You are fed from it, you return to it and become dust, until the time He wills to raise you and question you about all you have done, transgression and sin.

4Know now what you will answer at that time. Remember here what you have done, evil and good; weigh it and consider whether the evil is more or the good is more.

5If you have done more good, it is well with you, for you will rejoice and be glad in the resurrection of the dead.

6If you have done more evil, woe to you, for you will be repaid by the work of your hands: as your thoughts were evil, as you wronged your brother, and as you did not fear God, you will be repaid according to your deeds.

False Words and False Scales

7As you slander your neighbor and swear falsely by the name of God, you will be repaid according to your deeds.

8You make your word a lie and make it look true to your neighbor, though you know that you speak falsely.

9To those who stand with you, you hold that your word is true while you win their belief, and you multiply words where your word is not trustworthy and true. You will be repaid according to your deeds, as when you say, 'I will give you,' and do not give it to your neighbor, and slander your fellow.

10When you say with a pure heart, 'I will give,' demons lie in wait for you like dogs and make you forget it all; even if you took it and meant to give, they make you covet the goods of the world, to hoard what does not profit you and what you will not eat. For it says, 'They heap up, and do not know for whom they gather.'

11Again it says, 'The sons of men are liars; they falsify the scales; all of them go from vanity into vanity.'

12O people, do not go over into wrongdoing by false scales and false measures, by seizing another's goods and adding them to your own unjustly, by trespassing on your neighbor's property, and by all that you gain for yourselves and not for your neighbor.

13If you do this, you will be repaid according to your deeds.

14O people, do not trust in robbery, but live by what is right, by the work of your hands. Do not covet another's toil, to eat by robbery and plunder, without justice and right,

15which will not satisfy you when you eat it, nor profit you when you hoard it; you will leave it to another when you die.

16If your wealth grows, do not let your heart be proud. A little with righteousness is better than the great wealth of sinners, for the wealth of sinners is like smoke that goes out of the mouth of a furnace, and the wind takes it away.

Notes

  • v2 "a land of thorns and thistles, which He cursed because of you" — cursed is the ground because of you… thorns and thistles it shall bring forth for you (Genesis 3:17–18).

  • v3 "you return to it and become dust" — you are dust, and to dust you shall return (Genesis 3:19).

  • vv4–6 weighing the evil and the good — the dead were judged by what was written in the books, according to what they had done (Revelation 20:12).

  • v10 "They heap up, and do not know for whom they gather" — Psalm 39:6.

  • v11 "they falsify the scales" — Those of low estate are but a breath… in the balances they go up (Psalm 62:9); the Greek and Ge'ez Psalm reads "the sons of men are liars in the scales."

  • v12 "false scales and false measures" — You shall not have in your bag two kinds of weights… a full and fair weight you shall have (Deuteronomy 25:13–15).

  • v16 "A little with righteousness is better than the great wealth of sinners" — Psalm 37:16; if riches increase, set not your heart on them (Psalm 62:10). The wicked will perish… like smoke they vanish away (Psalm 37:20).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Day of Death
chapters.html:
3 Meqabyan 6

Those Who Meet the Soul

1Remember the day of your death, and think of what will come to you when your soul goes out of your body, when you leave your wealth to another and go on a road you do not know.

2Those who receive you are harsh, hideous to look at and fearful in their bearing. They will not hear your voice, and you will not understand theirs.

3Even if you plead with them, they will not answer you, because you did not do the will of the Lord your God; because of this they will terrify you greatly.

4Those who did the will of God have no fear, for the demons fear them; but the souls of sinners the demons mock.

5The souls of the righteous rejoice at the shout of the angels, for the angels gladden them greatly because they despised this world; but the souls of sinners are received by harsh angels.

6The souls of the righteous and the good are received by angels of mercy, for these are sent from God to comfort the souls of the righteous; but for the souls of sinners, harsh angels are sent from the devil to mock them.

Repent While There Is Time

7Woe to you sinners! Weep over yourselves before the day of your death reaches you, for after your death the days that have passed will not come back.

8Rather, before your days pass, repent while you are here, so that you may be free of sickness and pain when you come before God in joy.

9Let there be on you no evil shame, no ḥənqʷāqʷe, no love of luxury and food, so that it does not drag you into empty desire, which takes you far from God. For a soul filled beyond measure does not remember the name of God; the Spirit of life does not rest on it, but the spirit of the devil rests on it.

10As Moses said, 'Jacob ate and was filled; he grew fat, grew thick and grew broad, and forsook God his Creator.'

11His life grew far from God. For filling the belly beyond measure is like the neighing of a horse and like the wild beasts of the wilderness: eating and drinking beyond measure, and fornication.

12But whoever does not fill his belly stands firm on the foundation of God, like the wall of the horizon, like a strong building with a rampart. For it says, 'The wicked flee when no one pursues,

13but the righteous are bold as a lion.'

14Those who do not love God do not keep His word, and their heart is not upright.

15God gives them dismay and sorrow while they are on the earth, so that they have no rest, through fear and trembling, the plundering of their goods, troubles beyond number, and the chains on their hands from the hands of their masters,

16and through their own afflictions, which shake them, so that they may have no rest and may not live in peace.

Notes

  • vv2–6 the angels who receive the soul — the poor man died and was carried by the angels to Abraham's side (Luke 16:22). The harsh ones (ṣawwāgān) are the angels of the devil, as v6 says.

  • v3 "they will terrify you" — the Ge'ez yəfarrəhukəmu is "they will fear you," a slip of one letter for "make you afraid," which the verse needs.

  • v7 "Weep over yourselves" — Weep not for Me, but weep for yourselves (Luke 23:28).

  • v9 ḥənqʷāqʷe — a word not otherwise known; from the words around it, some kind of excess.

  • v10 "Jacob ate and was filled" — Jeshurun grew fat, and kicked… he forsook God who made him (Deuteronomy 32:15); the Greek reads "Jacob ate and was filled."

  • v11 "like the neighing of a horse" — They were well-fed, lusty stallions, each neighing for his neighbor's wife (Jeremiah 5:8).

  • vv12–13 "The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are bold as a lion" — Proverbs 28:1.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.
